title: Minimax Detection of Log Relative Risk Heterogeneity with Rare Outcomes and Rough Nuisances
banked_reason: D0.5.G tier=subfield < floor=field and NOT salvageable in scope; mathematical package passes, paper_score_ceiling 7 < 7.4.
gap_reasons: The delivered frontier concerns one scalar uniform-design class with known rarity and fixed nuisance/effect smoothness exponents, which limits its breadth and adoption case. The whole-null calibration and original-record rough-mixture converse are supplied; the matched-rate framing does not depend on an unfinished presolve step. Relative-risk heterogeneity is already an occupied target, so the novelty lies in this experiment's minimax rate and confounding crossover rather than the effect scale itself ([Shirvaikar et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.15793)). The description of the detector as usable for practical sample-size planning exceeds the supporting evidence: the conservative constants produce astronomical sufficient sample sizes, and no finite-sample power computations establish usefulness at realistic sizes. These scope and application limits constrain the projected leading-econometrics paper score despite completion of the stated theoretical kernel. [D0.5.G projected paper-score gate: paper_score_ceiling 7 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'field' is capped at 'subfield'. The score assesses the delivered research package without credit for unfinished work.]
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery derived matched original-cohort testing rates, exact composite-null calibration, lawful rough and oracle lower priors, saturation, and the supplied-propensity comparison. The mathematics passed D0.5, but fixed scalar uniform design, known rarity, fixed smoothness exponents, and lack of realistic-power evidence limited novelty to subfield below the required field floor. No Lean formalization was attempted; a material new program is needed to raise the tier.
tldr: For the stated primitive cohort class, the critical radius is, up to explicit universal constants, \(\min\{1,\max((n\lambda)^{-2/5},(n^2\lambda)^{-2/13})\}\), with explicit finite-sample tests and legal original-record priors. Supplying the propensity removes the second term; the radii are comparable exactly when \(n^{3/8}\lambda\) stays bounded, saturation occurs at \(n\lambda\le1\), and fixed-separation consistency holds exactly when \(n\lambda\to\infty\).
gap: The audited conditional-effect tests and higher-order estimation results do not settle the exact all-cohort decision problem for an unknown constant log-relative risk under a public vanishing outcome scale and arbitrary Hölder prognosis and assignment. The closest internal fixed-risk testing bracket lacks its rough converse; the failed matched retry retains a vanishing-occupancy cutoff and an unresolved upper refinement condition.
fill: The requested result determines an evaluable separation function, proves its two-sided critical-radius bounds for every public sample size and rarity, supplies total finite-null tests and a public nonempty-power regime, and identifies the precise same-parent supplied-propensity equivalence region. The proposal retains an explicit upper construction and an arbitrary-size analytic audit as supporting claims while leaving the global frontier answer open.
